answer: The protocol issues a cryptographic lantern token that vests rewards over a fixed schedule, and each vesting step demands a signed proof‑of‑work against a random tundra challenge derived from network entropy. Because the proof must be posted on‑chain each epoch, a new identity harvests only a sliver of the nectar reward per period while paying the gas and compute cost up‑front. An attacker flooding the system with thousands of Sybil IDs therefore incurs linear fees equal to all epoch costs, rendering large‑scale fake‑identity attacks economically infeasible.
